Fixed 'what'->'about' dramatically (82.6ms->10.4ms) and 7 other cases, but this branch handles many common stop/nasal-to-vowel pairs and 'prefer first over deepest' is wrong often enough elsewhere to cause severe collateral damage (10 new regressions, worst being 'be'->'in' swinging from -4.7/-3.7ms to +57.4/+58.4ms; full-benchmark MAE 13.121ms->13.156ms, within5/within20 both down). Structural gap, not a phonetic-category bug: every pairwise boundary-refinement loop in snap_boundaries_hybrid iterates range(len(refined)-1), so the very LAST word in a clip never has its end boundary touched by any of the (w1,w2)-pair logic -- it keeps whatever the raw CTC/VAD estimate produced. Reverted. Only 1 clean example exists in the current benchmark to design a more surgical version against (e.g. only correct when a LONG sustained gap separates the raw estimate from genuine preceding content) -- insufficient evidence to safely scope a fix without risking the same regression again. Revisit only if more last-word examples with this exact failure signature turn up.

'stuff' (ends in non-sibilant fricative /f/) into 'like' (starts with liquid /l/) hits case-4's own 'else: bnd=p_mid' fallback, same root cause as stop_closure_beyond_pmid_window_looked_like (p_start already displaced ~26ms past where HF-ratio genuinely decays to near-zero, confirmed via trace). Applying the EXACT SAME fix pattern (backward search from p_start for a sustained low-HF point, gated on w1 ending in fricative, mirroring the proven stop-closure fix) DID fix this case (69.3ms->16.6ms) but caused severe collateral damage (6 other pairs regressed 60-82ms: 'of'->'like'/'lady' x3, 'with'->'like') because THIS branch (case 4, fricative-into-liquid) is a much more common, frequently-triggered code path than case 14's rare final default -- many different fricative-ending words (of, with, stuff, etc.) reach it, each with its own decay characteristics, and a 70ms backward search window is wide enough to grab unrelated earlier content for several of them. Reverted. Lesson: the same 'raw estimate displaced past the true event, search backward' concept is not safe to transplant between cases just because it worked once -- blast radius depends heavily on how often the HOST case itself is reached, which must be re-verified per case, not assumed from a structurally similar fix elsewhere.

Attempted to rebuild the lost ensemble pipeline (silero VAD + pyannote + CTC/trellis posteriors + silence-trimming) that the user recalled fixing many errors previously. All four independently-tested components came back NEGATIVE against the full benchmark (MAE=12.764ms baseline, bench/results_current.json), each verified with a full run_align_benchmark.py + check_regressions.py pass before being reverted: (1) Silence-trimming before CTC forced-alignment (trim long pauses via Silero VAD, run CTC on trimmed audio, map back): mixed/no net win on 4 test clips (+/-5-10ms per clip, no consistent direction), despite trimming only 0.1-2.6s per clip. (2) pyannote/segmentation-3.0 frame-level speech-probability (loaded successfully once user accepted HF gating terms; direct model(wav) call on full clip bypasses broken torchcodec/ffmpeg audio decoding on this Windows setup): on the confirmed sonorant-junction dead-end case little/room (9.85-10.10s), speech_prob is completely flat (0.996-0.999) -- pyannote is a speech-vs-nonspeech detector, not a phone-boundary detector, so it has nothing to offer where audio is genuinely continuous voiced speech. (3) Live VAD-ensemble (Silero raw 32ms posterior + pyannote, averaged) as a corroborating AND-gate on the softest is_true_pause fallback branch in snap_boundaries_hybrid: exact null result -- predicted boundaries were BYTE-IDENTICAL to baseline (only align_time_sec changed, +1-2s/clip from the added pyannote pass) because RMS-quiet and VAD-silent are already near-perfectly correlated in this pipeline; VAD added no information RMS did not already have. (4) wav2vec2 CTC model's own frame-level "|" (word-boundary) token posterior, used to override the case-14 default p_mid fallback: first attempt used frame-CENTER time convention (bug -- caused systematic ~10ms/half-frame shifts, since align() elsewhere uses frame-START convention); after fixing that AND gating tightly (only override when peak probability >=0.5 AND >=25ms from p_mid), still net-negative or flat -- p_mid is itself CTC-derived (same model's constrained forced-alignment backtrace) and is already very accurate for the bulk of case-14 pairs; the unconstrained posterior peak is a worse estimate in most cases where p_mid was already good, and agrees with the ALREADY-known-wrong p_mid (not gold) in the one dead-end case checked (little/room: peak sits at ~10.03-10.05s, matching algorithm, not gold's 9.97s). CONCLUSION: the remaining ~55% of boundaries beyond 5ms tolerance are not explained by any acoustic-activity (VAD) or unconstrained-phone-posterior signal not already captured by the existing RMS/ZCR/voicing/HF-ratio/flatness heuristics plus the CTC's own constrained forced-alignment. They are dominated by (a) genuinely irreducible sonorant-junction/trailing-decay ambiguity and gold-label noise (see other entries in this file), and (b) a long tail of individually-diagnosable heuristic gaps -- i.e. the original one-error-at-a-time approach remains the productive path, not a bolted-on signal ensemble. All ensemble code (pyannote loading, compute_vad_ensemble, compute_ctc_posteriors) was fully reverted from forced_aligner.py to keep the codebase at the validated baseline.

yeah/indeed boundary: generic TRUE-PAUSE backward-scan for w2 start (the final else branch, not sibilant/whisper/um-uh-ah-er) is pure-RMS, walking backward until a sustained 30ms run below trail_thresh. "indeed" (vowel-initial) starts quietly/breathily after the pause -- RMS stays 0.002-0.011 (under trail_thresh 0.0098) through its first ~100ms, so the scan walks straight past the true onset to 1.1626 vs gold 1.0825 (80ms late). voicing DOES mark the true onset clearly (sustained 0.44-0.58 from ~1.09s vs a noisier 0.15-0.4ms baseline before it). Tried: treat rms<trail_thresh AND sustained voicing>=0.40 as NOT silence, for vowel/nasal-initial w2 only. Fixed indeed cleanly (80.1ms -> 2.0ms) but net-regressed the full benchmark (MAE 12.764->13.125ms, 18 regressed vs 3 improved) -- root cause: when the PRECEDING word (w1) itself ends in a vowel/liquid/nasal and trails off gradually, its own natural decay produces the IDENTICAL signature (low RMS + sustained elevated voicing) as a genuine quiet w2 onset, and the rule cannot tell w1-trailing-tail from w2-genuine-onset from voicing level alone (confirmed on clip9 idx33 "i": pred jumped 148.9ms too early, walking back through what was actually still "i've"'s own decaying tail). A depth-of-RMS-dip distinguisher does not cleanly separate the two either (the false-positive case actually dipped to a LOWER absolute RMS than the true-positive case at some points). Reverted. A real fix would likely need something that detects a genuine DISCONTINUITY (pitch reset, not just voicing level) between w1's decay and w2's onset, not attempted here -- pitch/F0 was already found non-diagnostic for a different (continuous-speech) category earlier this session, but was not specifically tested for this pause-adjacent scenario.

Given the prior indeed investigation already showed this branch is fragile to voicing-based changes (fixed one direction, broadly regressed elsewhere), not attempted further here -- would need to distinguish a genuine (if soft) word onset from a brief false-start blip, likely needing something beyond RMS/voicing level alone.

to/him: unlike most case-14 (p_mid default) errors, this is not a bad search-window choice -- raw CTC itself drifted BOTH words timestamps ~60-80ms late (to end raw=12.3008 vs gold 12.2772; him start raw=12.3609 vs gold 12.2782), so p_start/p_end/p_mid are all anchored to the wrong region entirely: p_mid=12.3408 lands deep inside hims OWN loud vowel (rms 0.09-0.11) rather than at the true boundary. Signal shows the true story clearly: silence 12.185-12.205, tos own weak vowel 12.21-12.26 (rms 0.01-0.02), a brief dip 12.26-12.28, then a sharp rise into hims loud vowel at 12.285+ -- gold sits right at the base of that rise (12.2782). w1 ("to") ends in a vowel, so it does not qualify for case-6s wide-window rescue (gated on NOT ends_in_vowel(w1), since case-6s closure-skip logic assumes a stop). A fix would need an analogous wide-window search for vowel-ending w1 too (e.g. steepest-rise detection over a widened window) -- not attempted here given repeated blast-radius fragility seen this session whenever case-14/case-6-style logic was broadened.

Tested hybridizing torchaudio MMS_FA (a different, purpose-built star-vocab CTC aligner, from the pulsar_from_scratch clean-room experiment) as a targeted fallback for the sonorant-junction dead-end category (was_still, little_room, gonna_react, regular_occasions, still_internal, be_a, and generally: w1 ends in vowel/nasal/liquid AND w2 starts in vowel/nasal/liquid). Per-case spot check looked very promising (gonna->react 78.7ms->20.4ms, be->a 70.6ms->18.3ms, second 87.1ms->20.3ms, your 64.9ms->12.6ms raw MMS vs our current tuned output). Implemented as: compute MMS raw alignment once per clip (star-interleaved), and for any pair matching the sonorant-junction phone-class signature, override bnd with the midpoint of MMS's own w1-end/w2-start estimate (gated on sane, bounded, positive-duration MMS spans). Full-benchmark result: NET NEGATIVE (MAE 12.491ms -> 13.644ms, every within-Xms metric worse, 235 boundaries changed: only 74 improved vs 123 regressed, some badly (up to 89.7ms), and it broke 2 previously-validated regression-suite cases). Root cause: the phone-class signature is FAR too broad -- it fires on huge numbers of ordinary continuous-speech pairs our existing heuristics already handle well (e.g. "surprisingly"->"restrained" at the very start of clip 0), not just the true dead-end cases, so MMS's noisier general-purpose estimate overrides many already-good boundaries. Reverted (compute_mms_word_spans, MMS_FA loading, and the override site all removed from forced_aligner.py). The underlying signal is real (confirmed wins on at least 4-5 known dead-end cases) but needs a MUCH narrower trigger -- e.g. only fire when our OWN case-1-through-13 logic genuinely found nothing (not just a phone-class text match), which would require threading a "no signal matched" flag through the elif chain rather than re-deriving the condition from word text alone. Not attempted given the refactor scope; a future attempt should start there.

A research agent was given the 3 open failure categories (sonorant-junction/repeated-word merges, long-pause boundary-placement convention, fast-speech function-word blending) plus the full list of hybridization techniques already tried and failed, and asked for concrete, testable, zero-new-training-data techniques. It proposed 6 techniques across the 3 categories, each grounded in real research (Pasad et al.'s wav2vec2 layer-wise analysis, formant kinematics, Stevens' acoustic landmark theory, corpus annotation conventions, CTC peaky-behavior literature, log-normal duration priors). Two of the cheapest/most promising were empirically tested directly against known cases (not just taken on the report's word) and both were falsified: (1) wav2vec2 Layer 8 (of 12) intermediate hidden-state frame-to-frame cosine distance, proposed as revealing latent phonological subspace transitions invisible to broadband acoustic signals. Tested on all 4 confirmed sonorant-junction dead-ends (little/room, gonna/react, be/a, was/still) using Wav2Vec2Model.extract_features(num_layers=8): the peak cosine-distance location was off from gold's boundary by 139-319ms in EVERY case, no better than the existing 6 acoustic signals -- multiple comparable-magnitude local peaks scatter throughout each word, not a clean staircase transition at the true boundary as the report claimed. (2) Flat silence-overhang constant for pre-pause boundaries, proposed as correcting for human perceptual lag / stop-release-burst attribution. Measured across the 10 documented trailing-decay known-hard-cases: stdev (67.6ms) nearly as large as the mean (-57ms), and critically the SIGN itself is inconsistent (8 cases end too early, 2 end too late) -- no single constant, or even a consistently-signed correction, can fix both directions. See research_agent_round2_all_negative_2026_09_22 for the 3 follow-up techniques tested next (CTC label-prior smoothing, phone-class-conditional overhang, relative-threshold HF micro-burst reasoning).

Follow-up empirical test of the remaining research-agent-proposed techniques from research_agent_round1_all_negative_2026_09_22 -- CTC label-prior smoothing (full implementation this time: divide emission by a global marginal token prior computed across all 14 clips, renormalize, re-run forced_align on the adjusted emission -- not just inspect posteriors), a phone-class-conditional (stop-specific) true-pause silence-overhang, and reasoning through the relative-threshold HF micro-burst variant. All three failed. (1) Label-prior smoothing: DID show a real, measurable improvement on RAW (unrefined) CTC alignment (MAE 45.68ms->43.31ms across all 14 clips, ~5% relative) -- genuinely different from the two flat-out-false Round 1 findings. But wired into forced_aligner.py (use_label_prior_smoothing flag, applied before forced_align) and run through the full benchmark, it net-REGRESSED: MAE 12.491ms->13.409ms (no-prelabel baseline for comparison, since the original 14-clip audio/*.wav files were replaced by a new project and had to be reconstructed from bench/raw_cache/*.npz), 153 changed, only 55 improved vs 98 regressed. Confirms the pattern already seen with MMS and CTC-pipe-posterior experiments: an improvement to the RAW CTC starting point does not transfer through the extensive heuristic refinement layer, because that layer was empirically tuned (search windows, thresholds) against the ORIGINAL, unadjusted CTC's specific behavior -- shifting the starting point breaks that implicit calibration even when the shift is itself an improvement in isolation. Reverted (LABEL_PRIOR constant, use_label_prior_smoothing flag, and the adjustment call all removed). (2) Phone-class-conditional (stop-specific) true-pause overhang: the original signal (3 known-hard stop-final cases averaging -55 to -90ms error) was a SMALL-SAMPLE ARTIFACT. Re-checked against the full population of stop-final true-pause boundaries across all 14 clips (n=40, using gold gap>=80ms as the true-pause proxy): median=0.0ms, mean=-4.9ms, stdev=23.9ms -- essentially unbiased. The apparent bias only existed because known_hard_cases.json by construction only contains cases already flagged as having large errors -- checking only that subset and finding 'a consistent bias relative to zero' is circular. Important methodological lesson for future bias-correction attempts: always measure against the FULL population, not just the already-flagged-hard subset, before concluding a systematic correction is warranted. (3) Relative-threshold HF micro-burst detection: not re-implemented -- reasoned through instead. The original absolute-threshold version's failure mode (HF-ratio numerically unstable, reading 0.4-0.97, at near-total silence because its denominator/total-spectral-energy collapses to near-zero noise-dominated territory) is not fixed by making the threshold relative-to-the-word's-own-peak instead of absolute -- a relative threshold rescales which unstable readings cross the line, it doesn't address the instability itself. The already-tried version already included an RMS-floor gate (>=0.3*trail_thresh) and still net-regressed after 3 tuning rounds; the relative-threshold framing doesn't change that mechanism.

summary: CTC forward-backward lattice-width (P(boundary-crossed) transition width, 0.2-0.8) does NOT distinguish sonorant-junction cases from sharp reference boundaries. Custom local forward-backward implemented from scratch (torchaudio only exposes Viterbi best path). Sonorant cases (little/room, gonna/react, be/a, was/still) showed crossing widths in the same range as sharp stop/fricative references in the same clips -- no separation. Mechanistically consistent with the CTC-entropy falsification from the same round: CTC's blank-dominant 'peaky' training behavior is a GLOBAL architectural property, not one that selectively relaxes at genuinely ambiguous phonetic boundaries, so no CTC-internal posterior-uncertainty measure (frame entropy, lattice width) can serve as a sonorant-junction detector.

Relative-to-own-peak HF-ratio threshold (rel_thresh = 0.15 * peak_hf, for non-sibilant fricative word-final boundaries before a true pause) was proposed as a fix for the earlier ABSOLUTE HF-threshold failure (HF-ratio numerically unstable near total silence). Standalone prototype looked promising on 4 hand-picked cases (kharouf, courage, drag, i've) but the prototype did not check the actual production gating condition (ends_in_fricative and not ends_in_sibilant) -- courage and drag don't satisfy it. Implemented properly in snap_boundaries_hybrid and full-benchmarked: net MAE flat (12.492 vs 12.491 baseline). Root cause: only kharouf/i've actually improved; 'aggressive' regressed to 101.1ms, an EXACT match to the already-documented nonsibilant_fricative_trailing_tail_true_pause_ive failure. Because peak_hf is near 1.0 for genuine strong fricatives, 0.15*peak_hf ≈ 0.12-0.13, numerically almost identical to the old absolute 0.15 threshold -- so this is not a genuinely different technique, just a rescaling that reproduces the same failure mode. Code implemented, benchmarked, and fully reverted (confirmed via grep and re-benchmark, MAE=12.491ms restored).

Montreal Forced Aligner (MFA 3.4.2, english_us_arpa acoustic model + dictionary, GMM-HMM triphone) tested head-to-head against the production wav2vec2-CTC+heuristic pipeline on 6 sonorant-junction cases previously confirmed UNRECOVERABLE by every acoustic heuristic tried (RMS, ZCR, voicing, spectral flux, HF-ratio, flatness, pitch) AND every CTC-internal signal tried this round (Layer 8 cosine similarity, posterior entropy, forward-backward lattice width, test-time perturbation). MFA WINS on 6/6 cases, often by a huge margin: gonna/react 38ms vs production 79ms (52% better), little/room 18ms vs 30ms (39% better), be/a 2ms vs 71ms (97% better), was/still 74ms vs 83ms (11% better), regular/occasions 7ms vs 69ms (90% better), still/internal 18ms vs 67ms (73% better). Average error reduction ~60%. IMPORTANT METHODOLOGY NOTE: initial run used fixed 0.6s context padding around each word pair and got wildly wrong results (500-900ms errors) on 3/5 cases -- root cause was the padding silently including untranscribed neighboring speech (disfluencies / tightly-packed adjacent words), which corrupts MFA's forced alignment since it must fit the given transcript to ALL audio in the window. Fixed by clamping padding to the nearest neighboring word's boundary. This is a MAJOR, actionable finding: MFA's phone-level triphone acoustic model (trained connectionist, not CTC) handles exactly the junction type our CTC+heuristic pipeline cannot, suggesting a genuinely different architecture (not another heuristic on top of the same CTC emissions) is what's needed for this failure category. Open questions before considering deployment: MFA speed/latency at production scale, dictionary coverage for out-of-vocabulary/proper-noun words, requires WSL/external process, and whether MFA's advantage holds on the OTHER (non-sonorant-junction) case categories too or is specific to this one.

Formant-trajectory kinematics (LPC via Levinson-Durbin, F1-F4 tracked over time, 2nd-derivative/acceleration magnitude as an articulatory-onset detector) does NOT separate sonorant-junction cases from sharp reference boundaries. Sonorant scores (little/room 717, gonna/react 66, be/a 772, was/still 1063) fully overlap sharp reference scores (share/tell 767, even/get 964, little/bit 198, beat/something 607) -- no threshold separates the two groups. 9th acoustic-domain signal tried (after RMS, ZCR, voicing, spectral flux, HF-ratio, spectral flatness, pitch, and this) to fail identically.

Multi-band energy-derivative landmark voting (4 bands: 0-500, 500-1500, 1500-4000, 4000-8000Hz; vote if a band's normalized derivative spikes >2.5 std near the candidate boundary) does NOT separate sonorant-junction cases from sharp references. Sonorant votes/4 = [3,4,3,1], sharp votes/4 = [3,3,4,3] -- fully overlapping, sonorant gonna/react actually got the MAX possible 4/4 votes. max_spike values also fully overlap (sonorant 5.2-11.4std, sharp 5.0-13.6std).

Whisper tiny.en forced-token cross-attention word timestamps (via whisper.timing.find_alignment, DTW over the model's built-in alignment heads) tested on all 6 sonorant-junction cases already tested via MFA. Whisper's timestamps were WORSE than the current production pipeline on 5/6 cases (little/room +147/+466ms vs prod 30ms; gonna/react +112/+111ms vs prod 79ms; be/a +108/+107ms vs prod 71ms; was/still +210/+208ms vs prod 83ms; still/internal -115/-115ms vs prod 67ms) and only better on 1/6 (regular/occasions -23/-24ms vs prod 69ms, but still far worse than MFA's 7ms on the same case). Consistent with known literature: Whisper's cross-attention timestamps are coarse (DTW over ~20ms mel frames and attention weights averages over many heads) compared to a dedicated phone-level HMM aligner. Only tiny.en was tested (fastest, matches this environment's CPU-only constraint); base/small might improve somewhat but MFA already provides a strictly better, already-working alternative architecture for this failure category -- see mfa_beats_production_on_sonorant_junctions.

Follow-up to mfa_beats_production_on_sonorant_junctions: tested whether MFA integration could lower the OVERALL baseline (not just the 6 cherry-picked hard cases). Built a full 14-clip MFA corpus (all 858 gold tokens), first as whole-clip utterances (blew up: MAE~75-57ms, worse matching artifacts, e.g. clip8 had a 3.66s internal silence MFA didn't expect and desynced the rest of the clip by ~250ms) then properly VAD-style segmented at gaps>0.5s (45 segments, matching how production already VAD-segments) -- this fixed the desync (852/858 words matched via proper LCS alignment, not naive greedy matching which also desyncs on transcript markers like '(())'). RESULT: full-corpus MFA MAE = 30.4ms vs production's 12.4ms on the same matched subset -- MFA is 2.5x WORSE overall, and worse on EVERY SINGLE one of the 14 clips individually. Production's heuristic refinement achieves sub-5ms (often sub-1ms) precision on the easy majority of boundaries that MFA's coarser phone-HMM (10ms-ish frame granularity) can't match. Then tested HYBRID gating (use MFA only on suspected sonorant junctions, production elsewhere) with two different gating signals: (1) linguistic rule (word1 ends in vowel/nasal/liquid AND word2 starts with vowel/nasal/liquid) -- 158/808 internal junctions flagged, but production STILL wins on the flagged subset (16.9ms vs 26.5ms), MFA only better on 59/158 (37%); (2) structural/introspective signal -- traced (via sys.settrace, zero modification to forced_aligner.py) which of 16 named cases in snap_boundaries_hybrid's CONTINUOUS SPEECH branch fired for each boundary, isolating case 16 (bare bnd=p_mid, the literal no-distinguishing-signal fallback, n=89) and case 13 (generic valley_rms<trail_thresh argmin, n=180) as the best candidates for genuine dead-ends. Production STILL wins on both: case16 15.6ms vs MFA 24.6ms (MFA wins only 28/89=31%); case13 11.6ms vs MFA 28.0ms (MFA wins only 44/180=24%). CONCLUSION: the original 6 dramatic MFA wins (gonna/react, little/room, be/a, was/still, regular/occasions, still/internal) were cherry-picked worst-case outliers from prior debugging sessions, NOT a systematically detectable class -- no signal tried this whole project (9 acoustic, 4 CTC-internal, 1 linguistic-phonological, 2 structural/branch-based = 16 total gating signals across the entire research-testing effort) reliably distinguishes 'MFA will help here' from 'MFA will hurt here' in advance. A full or hybrid-gated MFA swap is NOT viable with any tested approach. This does not rule out an ensemble/confidence-score-based approach (e.g. gating on MFA's own alignment likelihood rather than our signals) but that is untested and would need MFA to expose per-word confidence, which the TextGrid output does not include by default.

Round 4 research report (which included an explicit anti-fabrication protocol with Category 1/2/3 source tagging) cited 'the known failure case of/lot, which currently exhibits a 72ms raw start error' as the concrete falsifiable-prediction test case for its asymmetric label-prior gating proposal. VERIFIED: the word 'lot' does not appear ANYWHERE in the 14-clip / 858-token gold corpus. This case does not exist. The report tagged the surrounding reasoning as 'Category 3: inference/extrapolation' but stated the 72ms figure as if it were a concrete, currently-observed data point ('currently exhibits'), not clearly flagged as invented. Two OTHER Category-1 citations in the same report (Indic TIMIT corpus details, MAPS/Mason-Alberta sub-frame interpolation numbers) were independently verified via WebSearch and check out exactly -- so the agent is not uniformly unreliable, but the anti-fabrication tagging protocol did not prevent this specific fabrication from reading as an established fact. A third Category-1 claim (specific TIMIT NISTIR 4930 manual quotes about word-boundary DP rules, stop-closure-after-pause rules, and nasal marking) could NOT be verified: direct fetch of the actual PDF found none of the quoted passages (though the doc is scanned/OCR and this isn't fully conclusive), and web search found nothing matching either -- treat those quotes and the 'gold boundaries are DP-algorithmic not acoustic' conclusion built on them as unverified, not established.

Modified Group Delay (MODGD) phase-spectrum boundary detection (Round 4, Part 2) -- proposed as fundamentally different from all prior magnitude-domain signals since it uses phase instead of magnitude. Implemented from scratch (cepstrally-smoothed group delay with liftering, standard MODGD formula with gamma=0.9 compression). Tested the report's own falsifiable prediction: 'a distinct, trackable local maximum in the MODGD spectrum will occur within 10ms of the gold boundary' for sonorant-junction cases, contrasted with sharp reference boundaries. RESULT: peak MODGD-derivative magnitude fully overlaps between sonorant cases (961-3234) and sharp references (2067-5190) -- sharp refs actually score HIGHER on average, opposite of any useful separation. The specific 'within 10ms of gold' prediction held for only 1/8 total cases (both categories combined), with no advantage for sharp refs over sonorant junctions (offsets ranged -37.5ms to +57.5ms in both groups). Falsified -- the phase domain fails identically to all 9 previously-tried magnitude-domain signals (RMS, ZCR, voicing, flux, HF-ratio, flatness, pitch, formant-kinematics, landmark-voting).

Asymmetric label-prior gating (Round 4, Part 4): use label-prior-smoothed CTC (Path B, raw/unrefined) as an override for the production heuristic pipeline (Path A) specifically for TARGET_LEXICON function words ('of','lot','there','said','an','to','a') when the two paths disagree by >30ms AND local spectral flux is below a noise floor -- intended to selectively harvest label-prior smoothing's already-confirmed real improvement on raw CTC (45.7ms->43.3ms) without the net regression seen when it was wired into the full heuristic pipeline previously. Implemented and tested on the FULL 14-clip corpus (57 TARGET_LEXICON instances, not cherry-picked, per this session's established discipline). RESULT: gate fired on only 4/57 instances, and ALL FOUR were catastrophic regressions -- mean error on fired cases went from 3.70ms (Path A) to 131.90ms (gated). Overall MAE regressed 13.125ms -> 13.722ms. Root cause: when Path A (heuristically refined) and Path B (raw, unrefined) disagree by a lot, it's because Path B's un-refined boundary is simply unreliable, not because the label-prior sharpening cut through genuine CTC over-width. This is the SAME underlying label-prior-smoothing mechanism previously found to net-regress when integrated directly into the heuristic pipeline (12.5ms->13.4ms) -- confirms across TWO different integration strategies (direct wiring, and this gated dual-path approach) that label-prior smoothing does not survive contact with the production heuristic layer in any form tried so far. Note: the report's own worked example for this technique (of/lot, 72ms) was fabricated -- see round4_report_fabricated_of_lot_example.

User proposed: non-neural, classical alphabet-level inference at 1ms/2ms/3ms resolution (ensembled) instead of wav2vec2's ~20ms native frame rate. Directly tested the resolution component: recomputed the RMS/flux/HF-ratio/ZCR 'clarity' z-score (from clarity_analysis work) at 5ms, 2ms, and 1ms hop for the same 4 sonorant-junction cases vs 4 sharp references. RESULT: full score overlap at EVERY resolution (5ms: sonorant 0.89-4.52 vs sharp 1.31-4.00; 2ms: 2.17-4.26 vs 1.35-4.03; 1ms: 2.38-3.97 vs 1.77-4.93) -- no separation emerges as resolution increases, both groups just get noisier (shorter analysis windows -> less stable spectral estimates). Directly falsifies 'resolution is the bottleneck': raw audio is already 16kHz (0.0625ms native), and the production heuristic layer already searches sample-by-sample: finer feature hop doesn't sample anything new, it re-windows the same continuous signal more densely. On the 'non-neural classical alphabet-level classifier' component: this is what MFA (GMM-HMM) already represents, and it was exhaustively tested last round (mfa_full_integration_not_viable) -- full swap 2.5x worse, all gating strategies failed. A hand-built classical classifier trained on only the 14-clip corpus would have far less statistical power than either wav2vec2 (960hr pretrained) or MFA's trained acoustic models, so building one is very unlikely to beat an approach (MFA) already shown to underperform. Not fully implemented (a full classical-classifier build was assessed as low-probability given this direct evidence and deprioritized pending user confirmation).

User-proposed 'clean decode sliding search': for a candidate split point t between w1/w2, greedily decode wav2vec2 argmax tokens in [w1_start,t) and [t,w2_end) separately (free/unconstrained decode, not forced-alignment), score by edit distance to the KNOWN correct word text, argmin over a fine grid. GOLD-SEEDED (perfect w1_start/w2_end anchors) across all 813 internal (non-true-pause) junctions in the corpus: median error 0.00ms, 70% (573/813) land within 2ms of truth -- the single strongest result of the entire multi-session research effort. BUT 25% (202/813) wander AWAY from the correct answer even starting exactly there, up to 60ms off, because greedy-decode-edit-distance is monotonically biased toward extending w1's crop (truncated decode necessarily loses letters, so cost keeps 'improving' as you give w1 more time, past the true boundary) -- confirmed via direct trace on 'column'/'in': wav2vec2's own free decode of the ENTIRE span never produces 'IN' at all (decodes as 'Y'), so no split can achieve a true zero-cost match on that side; the optimizer just drifts to whatever minimizes distance-to-an-unreachable-target, which isn't the true boundary. This reveals the failure mode is the SAME fundamental acoustic-ambiguity wall as everything else this session (the model can't cleanly recognize the reduced word), just surfaced through decode cleanliness instead of acoustic features.

Same clean-decode-search technique tested with PRODUCTION's own current (imprecise) w1_start/w2_end as anchors instead of gold -- the realistic deployment scenario. Gate (requiring exact double match) opens on only 4/813 cases; using the raw argmin (ungated) result changes nothing (MAE flat). Also swept simulated 'rough hand-labeling' jitter (2/5/10/15/20/30ms) on the anchors: refined-boundary MAE degrades monotonically with jitter (4.53ms at 0ms jitter up to 11.93ms at 30ms) and at EVERY jitter level the refined result is worse than just keeping the (already imprecise) seed. No cost-threshold gate (tested 0/1/2/3) reliably isolates a trustworthy subset -- the gated-in subset's 'seed->refined' comparison gets worse at every threshold and every jitter level too. Conclusion: this technique's power is ENTIRELY parasitic on near-perfect (sub-5ms, effectively gold-precision) starting anchors; realistic hand-labeling precision (even a tight +/-5-10ms) destroys the benefit.

Reformulated version per user's explicit correction: don't require decode to match KNOWN correct text (removes dependence on foreknowledge of the right word -- user explicitly doesn't mind wrong word LABELS, only wants precise boundary TIMES). Two content-agnostic variants tested, both using PRODUCTION's own current w1_start/w2_end as anchors: (1) 'last change in whole window' (forward decode(w1_start,f) and backward decode(f,w2_end), take the last frame either changes) -- MAE 75.32ms vs production's 24.83ms baseline on this subset (675/813 worse, only 138 improved); (2) 'first plateau then change' per user's exact specification (scan forward, find the first sustained stable-decode plateau, place boundary within it) swept across plateau-length thresholds 1-5 frames (~20-100ms) -- ALL thresholds catastrophically worse (MAE 98-227ms, median 24-184ms), monotonically improving toward the 24ms baseline only as the threshold got so strict it mostly fell back to keeping production's own boundary (found=380/813 at the best-scoring threshold=5). Root cause: once the 'must match known-correct text' constraint is removed, the search has NOTHING to verify it's looking at the right content -- if production's own w1_start anchor (which defines where the scan window BEGINS) is imprecise by even 20-40ms, the 'first plateau' found can be leftover content from BEFORE word1 even starts, or a mid-word fragment, and the algorithm reports it with full confidence since nothing contradicts it. The known-correct-text constraint in the earlier (gold-seeded) version was doing all the safety work; removing it to avoid needing foreknowledge of the correct word also removes the only thing keeping the search honest. Confirms (a 3rd distinct way, after the MFA and label-prior attempts) that this whole research effort keeps finding the same wall: any technique that works well with perfect information degrades sharply and often becomes actively harmful once realistic imprecision enters, with no gating signal found (across bothrounds of testing, ~20+ signals tried total) that reliably distinguishes trustworthy from untrustworthy refinements in advance.

User-proposed 'sliding clean-decode' boundary detection: exhaustively explored across ~25 distinct configurations over multiple rounds of raw-data root-cause debugging (not hypothesized -- every claim below traced to actual frame-level argmax/probability/attention data). TIMELINE OF REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED: (1) content-agnostic scan anchored at word BOUNDARIES inherits contamination from adjacent words even with GOLD anchors (verified: gold 'harry' start lands on a frame still decoding 'D' from the prior word 'old') -- fixed by anchoring at word CENTERS instead. (2) 'last change until an arbitrary scan-limit' is a meaningless artifact, not a real signal (verified on 'mechanic'/'is': backward last-change was just revealing 'is'-adjacent words own letters, capped by scan boundary) -- fixed via first-plateau/pipe-based detection instead. (3) generic plateau-length thresholds cannot distinguish a genuine word-final stability from a normal mid-word phone's stability (verified on 'manage'/'to' and 'the'/'thing': the model's OWN letters take 2-3 frames per phone normally) -- partially fixed via 'trust pipe-adjacency directly unless multi-frame growth observed' adaptive logic (nthresh=2), which was empirically the single best configuration found. (4) even a CONFIRMED, both-directions-agreeing pipe position lags the true acoustic/gold boundary by 20-65ms on coarticulated finals (verified via direct softmax trace on 'didn't'/'even': P(pipe) jumps 0% to 93.7% in ONE 20ms frame with no gradual rise to exploit, and gold's own target falls literally MID-RECOGNITION of the word's own final letter -- not at any completion point the model ever represents). BEST ACHIEVED CONFIGURATION (adaptive fwd+bwd center-anchored, nthresh=2, simple average): 16.48ms mean / 10.90ms median / 42% within 10ms on the 120 true-blend (zero-silence) cases, vs production's 10.58ms mean / 5.60ms median / 65% within 10ms on the same population -- real, substantial, verified progress from the initial catastrophic first attempt (75-227ms), but does not surpass production. TESTED AND REJECTED REFINEMENTS (all measured worse than the nthresh=2 baseline): forward-only (26.4ms), backward-only (37.6ms), 2 hand-designed 'smart' override rules favoring the more-direct signal on disagreement (26-27ms both), 3-anchor ensemble with median/mean/trimmed-mean fusion (15.5-16.6ms, marginal/mixed), pure P(pipe)-probability-threshold triggering across 5 levels (16.2-16.9ms), combined adaptive+probability-threshold across 5 levels (16.1-17.4ms), acoustic (spectral-flux) fine-refinement hybrid within a narrow window around the coarse decode estimate at 4 window sizes (20.9-36.2ms, monotonically worse with wider windows -- confirmed via direct trace on 'mechanic'/'is' that flux peaks track unrelated later phonetic events, not the boundary). NEW SIGNAL SOURCE TESTED THIS ROUND: transformer self-attention weights (torchaudio's SelfAttention uses the fused scaled_dot_product_attention kernel which doesn't expose weights by default -- required monkey-patching the forward pass to manually compute and capture them). Attention-profile-change-peak (Layer 8, chosen for showing the most consistent signal in 2 hand-traced complete-merge cases: 'be'/'a' at 1.2ms, 'column'/'in' at 19.1ms) was FALSIFIED at full-corpus scale after fixing an indexing bug (emission.argmax computed on the un-indexed batch dim, collapsing frame_dur to the whole-clip duration and silently defeating the blend/pause filter) -- corrected result: 74.94ms mean / 51.31ms median / 14% within 10ms, substantially worse than both production and the decode-based approach. Attention-guided fine-refinement of the decode coarse estimate also tested (4 window sizes) and also worse at every window size (19.2-47.4ms), degrading further with wider windows -- same failure pattern as the flux hybrid. CONCLUSION: both available signal sources (CTC output head, transformer attention weights) have now been extensively explored with rigorous raw-data debugging; the CTC-decode approach (16.5ms/10.9ms/42%) remains the best of ~25 tested configurations and is a genuine, substantial improvement over doing nothing with this technique, but does not surpass production's existing acoustic heuristic on its target population.

Follow-up to the layer-8-only attention test: swept ALL 12 transformer encoder layers' attention-profile-change-peak signal on the full 120-case blend subset (layer 8 had only been chosen from 2 hand-traced examples, the exact 'don't generalize from a few cases' mistake this session repeatedly flags -- corrected by testing all layers fairly). RESULT: every layer fails decisively, 67-82ms mean / 37-77ms median / 4-20% within 10ms, vs production's 10.58ms mean / 5.60ms median / 65% within 10ms. Best layer (5): 36.90ms median / 20% within 10ms -- still far short. This is not a layer-selection problem; no layer in the network carries a usable word-boundary signal via this attention-profile-change metric. Combined with the earlier CTC-decode exploration (~25 configurations, best 16.5ms mean/10.9ms median/42% within 10ms) and the failed flux/attention fine-refinement hybrids, this represents an exhaustive, dual-signal-source (CTC output head + full attention stack) investigation of wav2vec2's internal representations for this specific boundary-precision task.

Tested the raw CNN feature-extractor output (model.feature_extractor, 7-layer conv stack, 512-dim, runs BEFORE the transformer/attention processes the audio at all -- a purely local acoustic representation, learned rather than hand-crafted, structurally closer to what a spectrogram-based feature would capture since CNNs have limited receptive fields unlike global self-attention) for consecutive-frame cosine-distance peaks on the full 120-case blend subset. RESULT: 78.50ms mean / 68.19ms median / 12% within 10ms -- worse than production (10.58/5.60ms, 65%) and worse than most attention layers too. This completes an exhaustive sweep of EVERY representational layer in the wav2vec2 architecture: raw CNN features (this test), all 12 transformer attention layers (attention_all_12_layers_falsified), and the final CTC output head (content_agnostic_sliding_boundary_comprehensive, best result 16.5ms/10.9ms/42% within 10ms). Only the task-trained CTC output head -- specifically optimized for character recognition, unlike the general-purpose CNN and attention representations -- shows any real signal, and even that requires extensive heuristic refinement to reach a still-below-production result. No layer of this model, at any depth, contains an exploitable signal for sub-10ms boundary precision on the true-blend (zero-silence) case population.

Deployed WhisperX on Modal (existing account, following the same pattern as the earlier CrisperWhisper deployment) and ran its wav2vec2-phoneme forced-alignment against gold text on all 14 clips (via restored audio directory, since original clips were replaced). Notably WhisperX's aligner uses wav2vec2_fairseq_base_ls960_asr_ls960 -- essentially the same base wav2vec2-960h model family as our own production pipeline. FULL-CORPUS RESULT (854/858 matched): WhisperX MAE=44.9ms/median=30.6ms/10% within 10ms vs production's 12.4ms/8.4ms/56% -- loses on every single one of the 14 clips, no exceptions. Better than the also-tested CrisperWhisper (93.6ms/2% within 10ms) but still far short of production. On the 6 known cherry-picked hard sonorant-junction cases specifically: WhisperX wins 4/6 (gonna/react 40ms vs 79ms, be/a 42ms vs 71ms, regular/occasions 12ms vs 69ms, still/internal 24ms vs 67ms), loses 2/6 (little/room, was/still) -- the SAME mixed pattern already extensively characterized for MFA earlier this session. Confirmed via full easy/hard split (479 cases where production <=10ms vs 375 where production >10ms): on EASY cases WhisperX is catastrophically worse (42.8ms vs production's 4.5ms, wins only 3.5% of individual cases); on HARD cases WhisperX still loses on AVERAGE (47.6ms vs 22.5ms) despite winning 24% of individual cases. This is architecturally the identical failure mode already established for MFA (mfa_full_integration_not_viable_2026_09_22): a differently-biased aligner that occasionally beats production on outlier-hard cases but is structurally worse on the easy majority, with the whole prior MFA investigation already having exhaustively shown (20+ tested gating signals) that no reliable detector exists to identify which case type is which in advance -- so a hybrid is very unlikely to work here either, without needing to re-run that full investigation.

CrisperWhisper (nyrahealth, large) forced_align tested on Modal (pre-existing deployment from earlier work) against all 14 clips' gold text. Full-corpus result (854/858 matched): 93.6ms mean / 66.1ms median / only 2% within 10ms vs production's 12.4ms/8.4ms/56% -- decisively worse across every clip, worse than WhisperX too. Not pursued further.

External research-agent proposal (Experiment #2, 'syllabic meter/ isochrony prior'): predict the internal w1/w2 boundary as a proportional split of the [gold_w1_start, gold_w2_end] zone, weighted by each word's CMU-dictionary phone count -- a purely linguistic/durational signal, zero audio analysis. Tested on the full 120-case true-blend population (same as every other test this session). RAW (undiscounted) result: 26.52ms mean / 23.30ms median / 23% within 10ms vs production's 10.58ms/5.60ms/65%. Root cause diagnosed directly from the worst cases (and/i 101ms err, didn't/even 87ms, the/same 79ms, you/know 68.5ms -- all short function words): canonical phone count badly overestimates actual duration for function words, which compress far more than content words under casual-speech reduction (a well-established linguistic effect). Tested a targeted fix -- discounting function-word phone counts by a tunable factor -- across 6 discount levels (1.0 down to 0.1); best point (0.7x) improves to 26.14ms/20.88ms/28% within 10ms, still far short of both production (65%) and this session's existing best decode-based method (42%). Lower discounts make it progressively worse. The linguistic-duration-prior approach has a real ceiling well below what's already achieved by other means.

Checked for a cheap calibration fix: traced (via sys.settrace, zero modification to forced_aligner.py) which of the 16 named cases in snap_boundaries_hybrid handled each boundary, then computed SIGNED (not absolute) error per case across all internal junctions. Most cases showing a large mean bias have mean and median sharply diverging (case 16: mean +6.45ms vs median +0.20ms; case 12: +7.90 vs +1.40; case 11: +5.39 vs -0.30), i.e. outlier-driven, not a uniform shift -- a blind offset would hurt the well-centered majority to marginally help outliers. Case 1 (sibilant-initial, n=48) looked most promising (mean -5.97ms, median -2.65ms, both negative) but per-instance inspection showed ~30 cases clustered tightly at -1 to +2ms, with the negative mean driven entirely by 5-6 already-known hard outliers (was/still -82.9ms, came/second -71.1ms, to/say -43.9ms). CONCLUSION: no safe systematic per-branch calibration fix exists; the heuristic's branches are already well-centered, and remaining error is case-specific, not a uniform miscalibration.

Final frontier test of combining all available independent estimates without training: production, MFA (segmented, the strongest alternate at 30.4ms), WhisperX forced-align, and the isochrony phone-count prior. Tested on all 813 internal junctions. EVERY combination loses to production alone (24.83ms/9.60ms/34.6% within 5ms): median(prod,MFA)=29.00ms, median(prod,MFA,wx)=28.41ms, median(all 4)=29.10ms, tightest-pair-avg=29.71ms, closest-to-median=28.74ms, drop-farthest-then-mean=29.97ms, tightest-pair-prefer-prod=28.08ms. Also swept an asymmetric 'only override production when the two weaker signals agree and diverge' rule across a 16-point threshold grid -- all 16 configurations lose. HOWEVER the ORACLE (best-of, per case) reaches 12.17ms mean / 4.47ms median / 52.8% within 5ms / 72.9% within 10ms -- vastly better than production's 34.6%/51.4%, proving substantial complementary information genuinely exists across the four aligners. MECHANISM for why it's unreachable, measured directly: in the 101 cases where MFA+WhisperX+isochrony all agree with each other within 20ms (apparently strong evidence), production is STILL more accurate (11.77ms vs their 16.57ms) and their consensus beats production in only 31/101 cases. Agreement among the alternates carries essentially no information about correctness because their errors are CORRELATED with each other (all generic, non-domain-tuned aligners sharing a common bias) and anti-correlated with production's hand-tuned strengths. This is the unifying mechanistic explanation for why all 20+ gating signals and every consensus rule tested this session failed: the headroom is real (oracle 52.8% vs 34.6% at <=5ms) but the selection signal does not exist in any combination of these estimators.

Whisper large-v3's OWN cross-attention DTW word timestamps (word_timestamps=True) deployed on Modal and benchmarked on all 14 clips -- the large-model version of the cross-attention hypothesis (only tiny.en had been tested locally, in an earlier round). RESULT: 199.62ms MAE / 138.50ms median / 0.0% within 5ms / 0.0% within 10ms, vs production's 12.05ms/8.20ms/32.5%/57.5% on the same matched subset (748/858 matched; lower match rate because it free-transcribes rather than force-aligning). This is the WORST performer of every technique tested this entire session. Whisper's native timestamps are structurally coarse (DTW over attention at mel-frame resolution, with segment-level chunking) regardless of model size -- scaling from tiny.en to large-v3 made it dramatically worse, not better. The 'bigger model with real language-model context will localize boundaries better' hypothesis is decisively falsified.

Direct investigation of whether the oracle headroom is EXTRACTABLE, using gold-free features only and AUC separability (measurement, not training). (1) ORACLE DECOMPOSITION: the gain is NOT noise -- production already wins 367/813 cases (no gain available), and 78% of the total oracle advantage comes from 143 cases with >20ms margins. A clean exploitable subset exists: 90 cases where production >10ms AND an alternate <5ms AND margin >10ms; perfect selection on those alone would move the <=5ms rate +11.1 points (34.6% -> 45.7%). Winner distribution across all cases: prod 367, MFA 181, wx 150, iso 115. (2) FEATURE PROBE for 'is production wrong by >10ms': SIGNAL EXISTS -- prod_gap_ms AUC=0.658, zone_dur_ms 0.652, spread_all_ms 0.637, prod_vs_iso 0.620, prod_vs_altmedian 0.611, prod_vs_mfa 0.610. Weak but clearly above chance. (3) THE DECISIVE TEST: stratifying by every high-signal feature (quartiles), the alternates are WORSE than production in EVERY stratum and alt_beats_prod never exceeds 41%. In the highest spread quartile production degrades to 53.80ms but the alternates degrade further to 70.61ms. The features detect CASE DIFFICULTY, not RELATIVE ESTIMATOR QUALITY -- difficulty hits all four estimators together, production least of all. (4) FINAL: conditional on production being wrong (n=394), an override would help in 54.1% of cases (a coin flip), and every feature's AUC for predicting 'override helps' is 0.429-0.483 -- AT OR BELOW CHANCE. CONCLUSION: the oracle headroom (52.8% vs 34.6% within 5ms) is real and concentrated, but the selection information is provably absent from every gold-free feature measurable here. 'Is this hard' is predictable; 'who is right' is not. This closes the rule-based selection avenue with a quantified negative rather than an assumption.

summary: HYPOTHESIS from the code audit: noise_floor=percentile(rms,10) and peak_energy=percentile(rms,95) are computed ONCE OVER THE WHOLE CLIP (forced_aligner.py:417) but every threshold derived from them gates a LOCAL 50-100ms decision, so on a clip with loudness drift every local scan is gated against a global floor. The code mismatch is REAL; correcting it makes things WORSE. Implemented PULSAR_LOCAL_THRESH_WIN_S: rolling per-100ms-block 10th/95th percentiles over a sliding window, interpolated to per-sample, used to normalize the envelope (so the 47 trail_thresh / 14 speech_thresh comparison sites stay untouched); the 3 absolute-RMS literals (0.0003, 0.0002, 0.0025) routed through an _abs_rms() converter. Full corpus: win=1.0s MAE 15.599 / 37.94% w5; 2.0s 14.737/39.74%; 4.0s 13.950/41.78%; 8.0s 13.045/42.25%; global (production) 12.491/44.46%. PERFECTLY MONOTONE toward the global limit -- wider is always better and the best is infinity. The global floor is not a bug, it is the right estimator; a local floor tracks the speech itself and destroys the speech/silence contrast the thresholds depend on.
technique_source: code audit of the threshold derivation block
verdict: falsified definitively; monotone, no interior optimum

summary: STRUCTURE IS REAL, FIX IS WORTHLESS. forced_aligner.py:1563-1567 forces w1.end and w2.start to a single point +/-1ms (a fixed 2ms gap) in the CONTINUOUS SPEECH branch, with only two narrow w2_start_override escapes. Measured on all 844 adjacent gold pairs: production collapses 78.6% of boundaries; gold gap is >10ms on 26.7% and >50ms on 18.1%. On the 59 collapsed pairs where gold has a >10ms gap the bias signature is exactly a mid-pause collapse -- w1.end too LATE, w2.start too EARLY, symmetric (gold gap 25-50ms: +19.5/-10.8; gold gap >50ms: +29.0/-27.2). BUT the gold-seeded oracle (hand it gold's exact gap width, keep the center it already chose) is worth almost nothing: corpus 12.491 -> 12.136 MAE (-0.355ms) and 44.46% -> 44.40% within 5ms (it LOSES 0.06 points). MECHANISM: the group biases cancel to a center error of +0.9ms, which LOOKS like the center is fine, but that is averaging -- individually the centers are scattered and large (clip2 i=27 'stuff'->'like' center off by +57ms; clip10 i=23 'came'->'second' off by -79ms). Mean |center error| on those 59 pairs is 14.02ms, statistically indistinguishable from the 12.5ms the system averages everywhere else. CONSEQUENCE: this retires the ENTIRE 'detect the pause and split the boundary into two' family -- no acoustic pause detector can beat an oracle that already knows the exact gap width, and that oracle is worthless here. NOTE: the first version of this analysis had a sign error in the oracle math (new_e1 = center - half instead of new_e1 = new_e2 = center); the corrected math is what is reported above.
technique_source: code audit of the single-point assignment at the end of the continuous-speech dispatch
verdict: structural description confirmed; as a lever, definitively falsified

(A) FORCED ALIGNMENT (/v1/forced-alignment, given the GOLD text = apples-to-apples with production), 1704 boundaries: MAE 40.357ms, median 29.250, w5 9.68%, w10 18.08%, p90 85.67, signed bias +18.64ms. summary: *** THE BENCHMARK IS PARTLY SELF-REFERENTIAL. *** curr_proj_golden_labels.json token ids are 't_<wav>_<n>', which is pipeline.py's own _build_injection_script format -- gold was extracted from the Pulsar editor AFTER our pipeline injected tokens and a human corrected SOME of them. The <0.5ms matches are a POINT MASS, not a smooth tail: in the integer-ms split the 0-0.5ms bin holds 27.2% vs 3.9% for fractional, while the adjacent 0.5-1.0ms bin is nearly equal (3.5% vs 4.1%). Easy boundaries would spread across 0-2ms; a spike below 0.5ms with a matching neighbour bin is self-match. It does NOT establish which subset is human-verified truth. The 1.0ms-gap group is provably not ours, but it could be an upstream machine pre-label rather than human work, in which case it is not ground truth either. ACTION REQUIRED BEFORE ANY FURTHER OPTIMIZATION: obtain a clean reference -- a sample of boundaries hand-placed blind, without seeing system output -- because until then the 5ms target is not measurable and every experiment in this log is scored against a partly circular target.

summary: Every per-case error table produced before 2026-09-23 (including case_attrib_full.json and the 'error is uniform across branches' conclusion) was MISATTRIBUTED. Four independent flaws in the sys.settrace approach: (1) it counted hits of a marker inside the CONTINUOUS branch and assumed hit k == pair k, but TRUE PAUSE pairs never reach it, so every pair after a clip's first pause got the wrong branch; (2) the dispatch has 16 branches, not the 14 named in '# N.' comments -- two unnumbered `c2 == "you"` elifs after case 3; (3) case 14 is a bare `else:` and the comment-based marker anchored on a NESTED if inside it; (4) pairs claimed by the two pre-passes (skip_pairs) and the is_pipe_gap early exit never reach the dispatch. Fixed in bench/trace_branches.py: reads the loop variable i from the frame, walks the real if/elif/else chain with the AST, labels pre-pass and early-exit paths, records the deciding `bnd = ...` leaf per pair, and exits unless every pair gets exactly one label.
